newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: ABN AMRO JAPAN TO ADD 70 ANALYSTS, DEALERS.
newsitem.headline: ABN AMRO JAPAN TO ADD 70 ANALYSTS, DEALERS.

text.p: Dutch bank ABN AMRO NV said on Wednesday it planned to hire 70 new dealers and analysts in an expansion of its capital markets activities in Japan.
AN ABN AMRO spokesman said the bank's ABN AMRO Securities (Japan) unit would hire the staff in the next six months as part of the group's Asian expansion plans.
"We are looking to expand because the climate for foreign banks in Japan is really improving," he told Reuters.
The spokesman said Japanese customers were becoming more prepared to use foreign banks as consumer confidence in Japan improved.
He said foreign banks also did not have to pay the "Japan premium", the margin that Japanese banks have to pay on their borrowings because of their debt problems.
"You can offer your services at more attractive rates because you don't have to pay the Japan premium," he said.
ABN AMRO earlier this year unveiled plans to spend $1 billion expanding in Asia and boost the region's contribution to group profit to 10 percent by 2000 from five percent now.
